A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work by the same authors. All 26 pages of each version, including equations, tables and appendices, support comparison; v1 contains Appendices A–B and v2 contains Appendices A–C.

before.justification: v1 reports mathematical bounds, proofs and analytical examples, including its Bayesian and infinite-dimensional applications. It reports no original experiments, simulations or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains entirely theoretical, including its expanded appendices. Its tables summarize analytical complexity bounds and mathematical constants, not empirical results.

M1.justification: The finite-step sampler changes: for step h, v1 Equation (7) uses state/score coefficients 2-exp(-h/2) and 2(1-exp(-h/2)), whereas v2 Equation (5) uses exp(h/2) and exp(h/2)(1-exp(-h)). The probability-flow ODE sampler and its Euler discretization in v1 Section 3.5 are also removed. The underlying OU process and score-training objective remain.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or conducts task evaluations. Gaussian-tail targets, bounded-support distributions and Bayesian posteriors are theoretical applications in both versions.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates empirical baselines against the sampler. Changes to the published theoretical bounds compared in Table 1 concern research positioning, rather than experimentally evaluated comparator membership.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, preprocessing, training budgets or evaluation procedures. Changes to admissible time grids and step-size conditions are assumptions of the theoretical analysis.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments or error studies. Appendix B.1 retains the analytical Gaussian-mixture illustration; changes to other theoretical applications and proofs are covered under T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The score-approximation error assumptions are analytical conditions, not statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Neither version reports empirical scores, measured rankings or generated-sample findings. The revised convergence and complexity expressions are mathematical guarantees, assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.3 and Appendix A.3 substantially replace the convergence argument with a martingale-based proof, changing error dependence and allowing grids controlled by their maximum step. Assumption 3 adopts averaged squared score error, distinct from v1's per-step condition and separate averaged RMS relaxation; the gradient relaxation also changes to a bounded time sum. Appendix B replaces assumed projection regularity with Lemma B.1 and adds explicit infinite-dimensional regularity and convergence theorems B.2–B.3 with derivations. The ODE theorem and Appendix A.9 proof are removed.

C1.justification: The headline square-root dimension and covariance-trace scaling claims remain, but the advertised extension to probability-flow ODE sampling is removed from both the abstract and substantive results. v2 also explicitly presents its modified convergence analysis as an alternative to conventional Lyapunov analysis, whereas v1 describes following a standard Lyapunov approach. Bayesian posterior guarantees remain in Section 3.4 despite disappearing from the abstract.

C2.justification: v2 adds a substantive comparison of Gaussian-tail assumptions with weak log-concavity and one-sided Lipschitz conditions, explaining the different decay bounds. After Corollary 3.11 it argues that exponential stopping-time dependence cannot improve without additional support geometry. Conversely, v1's dedicated limitations discussion is removed, including cautions about validating score assumptions and selecting an optimal practical stopping time.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies an implemented network configuration, empirical hyperparameters, hardware, runtime or code/data access information. The new Appendix C collects analytical constants rather than documenting an implementation.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through optimal transport, contraction theorems and Lipschitz transport maps along heat flows. It adds comparisons with newer weak-log-concavity and semiconvexity work, and Table 1 includes theoretical bounds from Li and Yan and from Gentiloni Silveri and Ocello. The introduction now distinguishes the paper through anisotropic noise and discretized generative flows.

P1.justification: The introduction, preliminary exposition and results discussion are extensively rewritten, with an explicit contribution list and reorganized assumptions. The standalone proof sketch, ODE section, limitations and broader-impact sections disappear. Appendix A is reorganized, Appendix B is substantially developed, and Appendix C is added.

P2.justification: Table 1 is reformatted, its caption shortened and its displayed comparison rows revised; the early-stopped-target result removed from the table retains a counterpart in the text. New Table 2 summarizes constants in Appendix C. Both versions retain a similar single-column layout and contain no figures.

improvement.justification: v2 improves exposition and research positioning and supplies a new main proof and fuller infinite-dimensional treatment. However, new Lemma B.1 omits the conditional gradient second-moment term from its Hessian identity, and Theorem B.3's proof displays a tau-order term where its conclusion requires tau squared. These issues affect the expanded theoretical justification, while explicit limitations are also removed. The benefits and mathematical concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
